claim: ELI5: after twelve cycles this campaign has still produced zero measured experiments. Cycle 12 did not die on a design flaw: HYP-0012 was pre-registered with both of cycle 11's fixes applied and was never executed, so there is no challenge record, no candidate file and no score. The campaign's failure mode is no longer physics and no longer inference rules, it is simply that no run has ever reached the scorer. This cycle therefore changes NOTHING about the science and adds exactly one thing: a guarantee that the run produces a scored verdict no matter what happens inside it. The design is HYP-0012 unchanged, restated in full so it is standalone: build the target from two payload keys, commit to it unconditionally, keep the circuit shape byte-identical to the incumbent's 35-CNOT block with the contract-mandated 8-Hadamard prefix (one-qubit gates, so the two-qubit cost stays exactly 35 and the cost penalty stays zero), fit the 96 angles to the target with an adjoint-gradient optimizer under a pinned restart floor, and read the verdict off a table written before the run that is exhaustive over (score, agreement band, convergence). The single addition is an execution guard: the multistart is deadline-aware, and any exception or budget overrun anywhere in the fit still returns a valid 139-gate circuit built from the incumbent's own seed-0 angles, with the failure recorded in the diagnostics. A cycle that crashes teaches nothing; a cycle that returns the incumbent circuit with a recorded reason at least keeps the ledger honest and costs one scored run. Formally: the candidate builds H_tot densely from payload['h_cost'] (leftmost Pauli label character = qubit 0, matching the sealed convention), commits unconditionally to T = normalize(expm(-beta*H_tot/4) @ payload['reference_state']) at beta = 3.0, which is CONTRACT.md's frozen Metric line read literally and therefore needs no Majorana algebra, no Jordan-Wigner choice, no kernel solve and no encoding enumeration, fits theta of shape (6,8,2) to T by simulating the FULL emitted circuit H^{\otimes 8} then baseline.block_gates(theta) from |0>^8 with an adjoint-gradient L-BFGS-B, emits [8 x h] + baseline.block_gates(theta_fit) (139 gates, exactly 35 logical CNOTs), and reports per instance its achieved self-fit fidelity F_self against its own committed T, the per-init (fidelity, status, nit, nfev, gradient-infinity-norm) table, the derived convergence flags, the cross-overlaps against three genuinely non-phase-equivalent alternative constructions, and the guard's status.
prediction: Score (mean over the five instances of s_i = 100*(1-F_i) + 100*max(0,(C2_i-35)/35)) drops from the incumbent's 99.6580 to 9.0 +/- 2.5, with valid=true and C2 = 35 exactly on all five instances (the emitted list is 8 one-qubit Hadamards plus the incumbent block, so the two-qubit count is unchanged at 35 and the cost penalty is identically zero). Specifically I predict per-instance fidelity at or near the sealed public F35 anchors (0.8955 Row 42, 0.9164 Row 48, 0.9011 Row 32, 0.9228 Row 30, 0.9229 Eq. 11), i.e. mean score in [6.5, 11.5], and the agreement test |s_i - 100*(1 - F_self_i)| <= 0.05 satisfied on all five (applied to the mean as the primary form, per-instance additionally whenever per-instance penalties are returned). Secondary in-path predictions (reported, never scored): GUARD_FIRED false on every instance; FIT_CONVERGED true on every instance (best init status 0 or ||grad||_inf <= 1e-6; at least 2 inits within 0.005 fidelity of the best; re-simulated F_self within 1e-9 of the best init's optimizer fidelity); F_cross < 0.99 against all three alternative constructions on at least the primary instance; emitted gate list length 139 with exactly 8 h, exactly 35 cx and no other two-qubit gate.
falsifier: Falsified if the blinded score does not fall below 90.0 while GUARD_FIRED is false and FIT_CONVERGED is true on every instance. That combination is a clean, identified refutation of the committed construction T = normalize(expm(-beta*H_tot/4)|I>) with H_tot from payload['h_cost'] and |I> from payload['reference_state'], under the contract's own H^{\otimes 8} reference prep: the optimizer demonstrably reached a converged, plateaued optimum of the exact emitted circuit against the state the candidate aimed at, so the scorer grades a different state, and the reported F_cross table names which enumerated alternative (if any) is the near neighbour. It is ALSO falsified, separately and separately recorded, if the score is <= 20.0 but the agreement test fails its round-off band (|s_i - 100*(1 - F_self_i)| > 0.05): the scorer then grades a state close to but NOT equal to the committed T, which is a partial-overlap finding and the starting point of cycle 14, never a confirmation. Any result with GUARD_FIRED true on any instance is not a physics verdict at any score (section 8 ROW G) and falsifies nothing. The verdict table in section 8 is exhaustive over (score, agreement band, convergence, guard) and is binding: no result of this run maps to an unassigned cell.
kill_threshold: This direction (fit the incumbent's frozen 35-CNOT topology, under the contract's H^{\otimes 8} reference prep, to a candidate-reconstructed target in order to reproduce the sealed F35 anchor) is DEAD if the score stays >= 90.0 with GUARD_FIRED false and FIT_CONVERGED true on all five instances. At that point the anchor is unreachable from any candidate-side reconstruction of the target under this payload, and the campaign must stop reconstructing and ask the Director for the sealed target's construction in executable form before any further cycle. Separately and explicitly: if GUARD_FIRED is true on any instance, or FIT_CONVERGED is false on any instance, the verdict is NOT a physics verdict at any score, the cycle buys nothing about the construction, nothing is recorded as a refutation, and the per-init table plus the guard's recorded reason alone decide whether the repair is MAXITER, more restarts, an emission bug in candidate.py, or a budget cut. There is deliberately NO absolute-fidelity fitting-failure floor anywhere (HYP-0011's 0.85 floor sat inside the normal restart spread against a ~0.895 ceiling and would have misclassified both a successful fit that landed low and a broken fit that landed high). A score in the open band 20.0 < score < 90.0 with the guard clear and FIT_CONVERGED true kills nothing: it is the pre-registered PARTIAL-OVERLAP measurement (section 8 ROW C/D) and fires reopen_condition clause (2).
brief:
CODER BRIEF (Codex-grade: every decision is already made; make zero judgment calls). This is HYP-0012's brief restated IN FULL so it is standalone, with exactly two additions (section 3.4 deadline-aware multistart, section 10 execution guard) and the corresponding diagnostics/verdict rows. HYP-0012 was pre-registered and never executed, so its design is untested, not superseded: do not redesign anything. The physics, the target construction, the circuit, the inference rules and the budget are byte-for-byte HYP-0012.

EDIT EXACTLY ONE FILE: workspace/candidate.py (create it). Touch nothing else. Do not read, list or reference anything under scorekeeper_private/.

=== 0. WHAT THE MODULE MUST EXPORT ===

Define prepare(payload) -> dict returning {'n_qubits': 8, 'gates': [...]}. Nothing else is read by the scorer. All diagnostics go into a module-level dict DIAGNOSTICS (section 7) and are also printed to stdout as one JSON line per instance prefixed with 'TFDDIAG '.

=== 0.1 IMPORT THE INCUMBENT TOPOLOGY, WITH A VERBATIM FALLBACK ===

The import of the sibling file workspace/baseline.py from candidate.py at score time is UNVERIFIED. Make it explicit and give it a verbatim fallback. At module top, exactly this, IN THIS ORDER (numpy first, because the fallback bodies use np):

    import os, sys
    import numpy as np
    sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    try:
        import baseline
        LAYERS, N_CHAINS, BLOCK_QUBITS = baseline.LAYERS, baseline.N_CHAINS, baseline.BLOCK_QUBITS
        block_angles, block_gates = baseline.block_angles, baseline.block_gates
        BASELINE_IMPORT = 'imported'
    except Exception as exc:
        BASELINE_IMPORT = 'inlined_fallback:' + type(exc).__name__
        LAYERS, N_CHAINS, BLOCK_QUBITS, ANGLE_SEED = 6, 5, 8, 0
        def block_angles():
            return np.random.default_rng(ANGLE_SEED).uniform(-np.pi, np.pi, (LAYERS, BLOCK_QUBITS, 2))
        def block_gates(theta):
            gates = []
            for layer in range(LAYERS):
                for q in range(BLOCK_QUBITS):
                    gates.append({'name': 'rz', 'qubits': [q], 'param': float(theta[layer, q, 0])})
                    gates.append({'name': 'rx', 'qubits': [q], 'param': float(theta[layer, q, 1])})
                if layer < N_CHAINS:
                    for q in range(BLOCK_QUBITS - 1):
                        gates.append({'name': 'cx', 'qubits': [q, q + 1], 'param': 0.0})
            return gates

The fallback body is a verbatim transcription of workspace/baseline.py (LAYERS=6, N_CHAINS=5, BLOCK_QUBITS=8, ANGLE_SEED=0, rz-then-rx per qubit per layer, cx(q,q+1) for q=0..6 after layers 0..4, 131 gates, exactly 35 cx, and NO 'h' gate anywhere). Record BASELINE_IMPORT in DIAGNOSTICS.

=== 0.2 THE REFERENCE PREFIX ===

Define, as a module constant:

    H_PREFIX = [{'name': 'h', 'qubits': [q], 'param': 0.0} for q in range(8)]

The FULL emitted circuit is H_PREFIX + block_gates(theta). CONTRACT.md assigns this prefix to this exact block twice verbatim ('every candidate prepares its own reference: the 35-CNOT baseline via 8 Hadamards to |+>^8'; 'prepare your own reference: 8 H for the hardware-efficient block'), and the sealed F35 anchors were refit under that convention. Hadamards are one-qubit gates: C2 stays exactly 35 and the cost penalty stays 0. Everything downstream (the forward sweep, the adjoint, F_self, the emitted list) uses the PREFIXED circuit. Never fit or measure the bare block.

MANDATORY IMPORT-TIME TOPOLOGY ASSERTION (runs in BOTH import branches): build blk = block_gates(block_angles()) and full = H_PREFIX + blk, then assert, element for element: len(blk) == 131 and len(full) == 139; the name multiset of full is 8 h, 48 rz, 48 rx, 35 cx; full[0:8] are h on qubits 0..7 in order; full[8:] is blk unchanged (identity of names/qubits element for element); every cx has qubits [q, q+1] for q in 0..6; and full[i] matches the expected (name, qubits) schedule reconstructed independently inside candidate.py from LAYERS/N_CHAINS/BLOCK_QUBITS plus the 8-H prefix. Any mismatch raises RuntimeError at import.

=== 1. BUILD THE TARGET (COMMITTED UNCONDITIONALLY, NO SELECTION, NO SWITCHING) ===

1.1 Dense Hamiltonian from Pauli strings. Write pauli_to_dense(label, coeff) using the convention LEFTMOST LABEL CHARACTER = QUBIT 0 = MOST SIGNIFICANT tensor factor: dense = coeff * kron(P[label[0]], kron(P[label[1]], ...)) with P = {'I':I2,'X':X,'Y':Y,'Z':Z}. H_tot = sum over payload['h_cost'] of pauli_to_dense(label, coeff). Assert H_tot.shape == (256,256) and ||H_tot - H_tot^dagger||_inf < 1e-10.

1.2 Committed target. T_raw = scipy.linalg.expm(-payload['beta'] * H_tot / 4.0) @ np.asarray(payload['reference_state'], dtype=complex).ravel(); T = T_raw / norm(T_raw). This is CONTRACT.md's Metric line read literally (exact TFD = e^{-beta H_tot/4}|I>, H_tot = H_L + H_R). Apply the CONTRACT gauge fix (rotate the largest-modulus amplitude real positive) to T for provenance only; fidelity |<T|psi>|^2 is phase-blind, so this cannot move the score, and no phase-equivalent variant appears anywhere in the decision table. There is NO enumeration, NO elimination, NO switching: whatever section 6's diagnostics say, T as defined here is what is fitted and what is emitted against.

1.3 FIRST-CALL CROSS-CHECK. On the FIRST prepare() call of the process, regardless of payload['name'] (do NOT gate on the name string), recompute exp(-beta*H_tot/4)|I> a second way: eigen-decompose H_tot (numpy.linalg.eigh), form U @ diag(exp(-beta*w/4)) @ U^dagger @ |I>, normalize, and assert fidelity with T > 1 - 1e-10. Record payload['name'] as DIAGNOSTICS['first_call_name'] and the check result as DIAGNOSTICS['expm_crosscheck_ok'].

=== 2. SIMULATOR AND ADJOINT GRADIENT ===

2.1 Statevector over 8 qubits as a length-256 complex array, qubit 0 = most significant bit of the index. Implement apply_h(psi,q), apply_rz(psi,q,th), apply_rx(psi,q,th), apply_cx(psi,c,t) by index arithmetic (reshape to (2,)*8, slicing), NOT by building 256x256 matrices. Rotations are exp(-i*theta*P/2), matching the contract. Hadamard is the standard (X+Z)/sqrt(2).

2.2 Forward: psi0 = H_PREFIX applied to |0>^8 (the basis vector with index 0); this equals |+>^8 and is PARAMETER-FREE, so compute it once per process and cache it. psi(theta) = block_gates(theta) applied in order to psi0. Objective f(theta) = 1 - |<T|psi(theta)>|^2.

2.3 Gradient by the accumulate-before-undo adjoint, over the BLOCK GATES ONLY (the 8 H are parameter-free and the reverse sweep stops at psi0): run the forward sweep storing nothing but the final state; set lam = -2 * conj(<T|psi>) * T (verify the sign by the finite-difference gate below, not by argument); sweep the block gates in REVERSE, at each gate first undoing it on psi (apply the inverse gate), then for a parametrized gate computing dpsi/dtheta = (-i/2) * P applied to the (now pre-gate) psi and taking grad_k = 2*Re(<lam| dpsi/dtheta>), then undoing the gate on lam as well. IMPORT-TIME FINITE-DIFFERENCE GATE (mandatory): on a random normalized 256-dim target and random theta from default_rng(7), starting from the SAME cached psi0 = |+>^8, check max |grad_adjoint - grad_FD| < 1e-6 with central differences at h = 1e-5 over 12 randomly chosen coordinates; raise RuntimeError on failure. Record DIAGNOSTICS['grad_check_maxerr'].

=== 3. THE FIT ===

scipy.optimize.minimize(f, theta.ravel(), jac=grad, method='L-BFGS-B', options={'maxiter': MAXITER, 'ftol': 0.0, 'gtol': 1e-10}). Multi-start: init 0 is block_angles() (the deterministic seed-0 draw, so the run's worst case is the incumbent's own starting point); inits 1..N_INITS-1 are default_rng(1000 + instance_index*100 + k).uniform(-pi, pi, (6,8,2)). Keep the argmax-fidelity result. Emit H_PREFIX + block_gates(theta_best.reshape(6,8,2)).

3.1 RESTART FLOOR FIRST (pinned before the run, not adaptive): N_INITS = 6 is a FLOOR and is never reduced by the clock except by the section-3.4 deadline, which is recorded. MAXITER starts at 3000 and is the ONLY quantity the clock may reduce, never below 400. Measure the cost of one objective+gradient evaluation once at import (time 20 evaluations, take the median) and record it; set MAXITER = clip(int(0.6 * PER_INSTANCE_CAP_S / (6 * 2.0 * median_eval_s)), 400, 3000), then PIN it as a module constant for the whole process (computed once, never recomputed per instance). The factor 2.0 accounts for L-BFGS-B line search making nfev exceed nit by roughly 1.2x-2x.

3.2 BUDGET PROVENANCE: TOTAL_BUDGET_S = 900 and PER_INSTANCE_CAP_S = 150 are SELF-IMPOSED caps, not a known scorer wall clock. The scorer's per-candidate time limit is not documented in CONTRACT.md, so exceeding it is a scorer-side risk this cycle accepts knowingly. State exactly that in a comment at the constants. Record wall time per instance.

3.3 PER-INIT RECORD AND THE DERIVED CONVERGENCE FLAGS. For every init k record final fidelity F_k, scipy status, nit, nfev and final ||grad||_inf, and put the full list in DIAGNOSTICS. Then compute, per instance, these four booleans and record every one of them (pure functions of the record above plus F_self from section 4; all thresholds pinned here, before the run, and none of them a fidelity VALUE):

    best_k              = argmax_k F_k
    conv_best           = (status[best_k] == 0) or (gradinf[best_k] <= 1e-6)
    conv_plateau        = (number of k with F_k >= F_best - 0.005) >= 2
    conv_resim          = abs(F_self - F_best) <= 1e-9
    FIT_CONVERGED       = conv_best and conv_plateau and conv_resim

conv_best says the winning restart stopped at a stationary point, not out of iterations. conv_plateau says the multistart found the same optimum twice. conv_resim says the independently re-simulated emitted circuit reproduces the optimizer's own fidelity, so the reported number belongs to the circuit actually emitted. FIT_CONVERGED, not any fidelity threshold, is what section 8 reads. Also record, as observation only, F_self minus the PUBLIC CONTRACT.md F35 anchor for that instance (anchor_delta); the anchors are public and this is a reported comparison, never an input to any selection, flag or emitted circuit.

3.4 DEADLINE-AWARE MULTISTART (ADDITION 1, the only change to the fit). Record t_start = time.monotonic() at entry to prepare(). Before LAUNCHING init k (k >= 1, never before init 0), check elapsed = time.monotonic() - t_start; if elapsed > 0.8 * PER_INSTANCE_CAP_S, stop launching further inits, break out of the multistart loop, and record inits_run = k and deadline_hit = True. Init 0 is ALWAYS run to completion: it is the incumbent's own seed-0 starting point and guarantees a meaningful result. Do NOT interrupt an init already in flight (scipy has no clean interrupt here; a partially-run init has no recorded status and must not enter the per-init table). Record inits_run and deadline_hit per instance. Note the interaction, which is intended and needs no extra rule: if inits_run < 2 then conv_plateau is false by its own definition, FIT_CONVERGED is false, and section 8 ROW F fires, so a clock-truncated run can never be read as a physics verdict.

=== 4. SELF-FIT FIDELITY AND THE AGREEMENT TEST ===

After choosing theta_best, RE-SIMULATE THE EMITTED GATE LIST FROM SCRATCH FROM |0>^8, including the 8 Hadamards, without reusing any optimizer state or the cached psi0, and compute F_self = |<T|psi_emitted>|^2. This number is the point of the cycle: the fidelity of the EXACT circuit emitted against the EXACT state committed to. Record F_self per instance.

If the scorer's sealed target equals the committed T, then s_i == 100*(1 - F_self_i) EXACTLY up to simulator round-off, because both numbers are the fidelity of the same emitted circuit against the same state and the cost penalty is identically zero at C2 = 35. This is an identity, not an approximation, so its tolerance is round-off, not a physics band. Pinned bands, checked in this order:

    d_i = |s_i - 100*(1 - F_self_i)|
    AGREE_EXACT    : d_i <= 0.05   on every instance   (0.05 score points = 5e-4 in fidelity, half the promotion margin, and still far looser than the ~1e-9 round-off of a 256-dimensional statevector simulation, so it cannot fire spuriously)
    AGREE_NEARMISS : 0.05 < d_i <= 1.0 on any instance  (its own recorded outcome: the sealed target is CLOSE BUT NOT EQUAL to T)
    AGREE_FAIL     : d_i > 1.0 on any instance

Read s_i from the scorekeeper verdict. The MEAN form is primary because it is the one number the verdict is guaranteed to carry: apply the identical bands to |score - 100*(1 - mean_i F_self_i)|. Apply the per-instance form additionally whenever per-instance penalties are returned, and record both.

=== 5. COST SAFETY ===

Assert before returning: len(gates) == 139; exactly 8 gates named 'h', on qubits 0..7, at indices 0..7; exactly 35 two-qubit gates, all 'cx'; no other two-qubit gate name present. This assertion runs on BOTH the fitted return path and the section-10 guard path. If it fails on the fitted path, fall through to the guard (section 10). If it fails on the guard path, raise RuntimeError.

=== 6. DIAGNOSTIC-ONLY ALTERNATIVES AND COUNTS (nothing is switched by these) ===

Compute and record, per instance, F_cross = |<T|m>|^2 for the three genuinely non-phase-equivalent alternatives: m1 = normalize(expm(-beta * payload['h_left'] / 2) @ |I>); m2 = normalize(expm(-beta * H_tot / 8) @ |I>); m3 = normalize(expm(-beta * H_tot / 2) @ |I>). OBSERVATION ONLY: they never touch theta, T, or the emitted circuit. Also record n_h_cost = len(payload['h_cost']), K = payload['K'], and h_cost_count_ok = (n_h_cost == 2*K).

=== 7. DIAGNOSTICS PAYLOAD (one JSON line per instance, stdout, prefix 'TFDDIAG ') ===

name, baseline_import, first_call_name, expm_crosscheck_ok, grad_check_maxerr, median_eval_s, MAXITER, N_INITS, inits_run, deadline_hit, GUARD_FIRED, guard_reason, per-init list of (F_k, status, nit, nfev, gradinf), best_k, F_best, F_self, conv_best, conv_plateau, conv_resim, FIT_CONVERGED, anchor_delta, F_cross_m1/m2/m3, n_h_cost, K, h_cost_count_ok, wall_s, n_gates (139), n_h (8), c2_count (35). The TFDDIAG line must be printed on EVERY path, including the guard path; on the guard path the fields that were never computed are emitted as null.

=== 8. THE PRE-REGISTERED VERDICT TABLE (EXHAUSTIVE OVER (score, agreement band, convergence, guard)) ===

Let S be the blinded mean score, A in {AGREE_EXACT, AGREE_NEARMISS, AGREE_FAIL} the section-4 band, C = (FIT_CONVERGED on all five instances), G = (GUARD_FIRED on any instance). Every (S, A, C, G) falls in exactly one row; nothing here is decided after the run.

ROW G (checked FIRST, overrides everything): G is true, at any S, A, C. Verdict = EXECUTION FAILURE, not a physics verdict. guard_reason names the repair. Nothing is confirmed or refuted. Expected S in this row is ~99.658 on the guarded instances, since the guard emits the incumbent's seed-0 angles with the H prefix.

ROW F (checked SECOND): C is false with G false, at any S and any A. Verdict = FITTING FAILURE, not a physics verdict. Nothing is confirmed, nothing is refuted, the construction question is untouched. Which flag failed names the repair: conv_best false with status 1 and gradinf > 1e-6 on most inits means the repair is MAXITER; conv_plateau false because inits_run < 2 or deadline_hit true means the repair is the clock (cut PER_INSTANCE_CAP_S or MAXITER, keep the restart floor); conv_plateau false with status 0 and spread-out fidelities means more restarts; conv_resim false is a simulator/emission bug in candidate.py itself and is fixed before any further inference.

ROW A: S <= 20.0, A = AGREE_EXACT, C true, G false. Verdict = CONSTRUCTION CONFIRMED. If additionally S is in [6.5, 11.5] the sealed F35 anchor is reproduced to the digit and the scorer's target construction and start state are both confirmed in one run; the campaign moves to the DIRECTION's actual question (ma-QAOA + SAP/OSAP against F35 at matched cost) in cycle 14. If 11.5 < S <= 20.0 the construction is confirmed but the anchor is not reproduced, and cycle 14 is a fit-budget cycle (raise MAXITER/N_INITS on the same committed T), not a construction cycle.

ROW B: S <= 20.0, A = AGREE_NEARMISS or AGREE_FAIL, C true, G false. Verdict = CLOSE BUT NOT EQUAL. The scorer grades a state at high but sub-unit overlap with T, quantified by d. Recorded as a partial-overlap measurement, never as a confirmation. Cycle 14 takes the F_cross table's nearest alternative as its committed T with no re-argument.

ROW C: 20.0 < S < 90.0, A = AGREE_EXACT, C true, G false. Verdict = PARTIAL OVERLAP, a measured statement that the sealed target overlaps the committed T at approximately 1 - S/100. The agreement test cannot see an ansatz-power deficit, so this band is jointly consistent with a partially-wrong construction and with a genuine ansatz shortfall; the F_cross table and anchor_delta discriminate. Fires reopen_condition clause (2).

ROW D: 20.0 < S < 90.0, A = AGREE_NEARMISS or AGREE_FAIL, C true, G false. Verdict = SCORER AND SELF-FIT DISAGREE. The blinded s_i is trusted and F_self is advisory (harness rule 3). Cycle 14's first action is to re-derive the emitted-circuit simulation convention (qubit ordering, gate parameter sign) against the contract, because a disagreement at fixed circuit and fixed state is a simulator-convention mismatch, not a physics result.

ROW E: S >= 90.0, C true, G false (A's band is recorded but does not change the row). Verdict = FALSIFIED / DEAD per kill_threshold. The committed construction is refuted with identification, the F_cross table names the near neighbour if any, and the campaign asks the Director for the sealed target in executable form.

=== 9. WHAT NOT TO DO ===

No Majorana algebra, no Jordan-Wigner reconstruction, no kernel solve, no encoding enumeration: that machinery is deleted on purpose and its reintroduction is the HYP-0008 index-range defect. No structural change to the 35-CNOT block (not one two-qubit gate added, removed or moved); the ONLY circuit change relative to the incumbent is the parameter-free 8-Hadamard prefix that CONTRACT.md mandates. No absolute-fidelity fitting-failure threshold anywhere in the code or the reporting. No use of anchor_delta or F_cross to select, switch or gate anything. No attempt to infer or read the hidden battery. No selection among target constructions. No self-reported score.

=== 10. EXECUTION GUARD (ADDITION 2; the reason this cycle exists) ===

The campaign has completed twelve cycles with zero measured experiments. A candidate that raises at score time produces nothing; a candidate that returns the incumbent circuit with a recorded reason produces a scored row and a named repair. Therefore wrap the ENTIRE body of prepare() (target build, fit, self-fit, diagnostics) in one try/except Exception. On any exception:

    GUARD_FIRED  = True
    guard_reason = type(exc).__name__ + ': ' + str(exc)[:200] + ' | ' + the last traceback frame (file:line)
    theta_guard  = block_angles()            # the incumbent's own deterministic seed-0 angles
    gates        = H_PREFIX + block_gates(theta_guard)

run the section-5 assertion on that list (raising RuntimeError only if it fails here), print the TFDDIAG line with the computed fields and nulls elsewhere, and RETURN {'n_qubits': 8, 'gates': gates}. Also set GUARD_FIRED on the non-exception budget path: if wall time for the instance exceeds PER_INSTANCE_CAP_S at the moment the fit finishes, still return the FITTED circuit (it is strictly better than the guard circuit) but record GUARD_FIRED = True with guard_reason = 'budget_overrun:<seconds>', because the run then carries a scorer-side timeout risk and must not be read as a clean physics verdict. The import-time gates of sections 0.1 and 2.3 are deliberately NOT inside the guard: an import-time failure is a code defect that must be visible immediately, not papered over with the incumbent circuit.
done_definition: workspace/candidate.py exists and, on `python -c 'import candidate'` from workspace/, passes all four import-time gates (the element-for-element 139-gate prefixed topology assertion including the 131-gate block substring, the adjoint finite-difference gate < 1e-6 measured from |+>^8, the eval-timing measurement, the MAXITER pinning) with no exception. A local smoke run of prepare() on a hand-built payload (any h_cost Pauli list of the right shape, any h_left of shape (256,256), any normalized reference_state) returns {'n_qubits': 8, 'gates': [...]} with exactly 139 gates, the first 8 being 'h' on qubits 0..7, exactly 35 'cx' and no other two-qubit gate, and emits one TFDDIAG JSON line carrying every field in section 7, including baseline_import, inits_run, deadline_hit, GUARD_FIRED, guard_reason, the per-init table, best_k, F_best, F_self, all four convergence flags, anchor_delta, F_cross_m1/m2/m3 and h_cost_count_ok. A SECOND smoke run with a deliberately corrupted payload (e.g. reference_state of the wrong length) must NOT raise: it must return a valid 139-gate guard circuit with GUARD_FIRED true and a non-empty guard_reason, and still print its TFDDIAG line. The convergence flags are computed only from the per-init record and F_self, with no fidelity threshold anywhere in their definitions, and conv_resim is True on the clean smoke run. The scorer then returns valid=true on all five instances with C2 = 35 on each. No file outside workspace/candidate.py is modified.
reopen_condition: This direction reopens only on one of five specific new facts. (1) The Director publishes the sealed target's construction in executable form (the exact expression and the exact start state the scorer simulates from), in which case the fit is re-run against that expression with the same pinned budget and the anchor reproduction is decided in one cycle. (2) A verdict lands in section 8 ROW B, C, D or E (FIT_CONVERGED true on all five, guard clear, with either score > 20.0 or an agreement band worse than AGREE_EXACT) AND the recorded F_cross table shows one of m1/m2/m3 at overlap >= 0.99 with the state implied by the measured numbers (|<T|sealed>|^2 approximately 1 - S/100 in ROW C/D, approximately 1 - d/100 in ROW B), in which case that named alternative becomes the committed T of the next cycle, with no re-argument. (3) h_cost_count_ok is recorded False, i.e. len(payload['h_cost']) != 2*K, meaning payload['h_cost'] is not H_L + H_R as CONTRACT.md states and the target construction rests on a misread key; that is a Director question, not a cycle. (4) A Director statement or scorer-side artifact establishes that the sealed F35 anchors were fit WITHOUT the H^{\otimes 8} prefix, contradicting CONTRACT.md's two verbatim statements, in which case the prefix is removed and the fit re-run unchanged otherwise. (5) The run lands in ROW G or ROW F, i.e. it again fails to produce a physics verdict: then the reopening spec is mechanical and not a redesign, namely re-run this identical hypothesis with the single quantity named by guard_reason or by the failing convergence flag changed (PER_INSTANCE_CAP_S, MAXITER, or the emission bug fixed), and nothing else touched. Absent one of these five, do not propose another candidate-side reconstruction of the target.
